div.head: II Cn 67
div.ab: And gif hwa wylle georne fram unrihte gecirran eft to rihte, miltsige man for Godes ege, swa man best mæge, þam swyþe georne.
⁊ gif hwa wille georne fram unrihte gecyrran eft to rihte, miltsige mann for Godes ege, swa man best mage, þam swiðe georne.
Et si aliquis uelit ab iniusticia reuerti ad rectum, remittatur ei pro timore Dei, sicut melius poterit.
Gyf hwa wille georne fram unrihte to rihte gecyrran, mildsige man him for Godes ege, swa man betst mæge, ðam men swyðe georne.
And gif hwa wylle georne fram unrihte gecirran eft to rihte, miltsige man for Godes ege, swa man betst mæge, þam swyþe georne.
If anyone zealously desires to turn from lawlessness to observance of the law, as great mercy as possible shall be shown to him, with the utmost readiness, through the fear of God.
And if anyone sincerely desires to turn from lawlessness to justice, as much mercy as possible must be shown to him with very great eagerness, for fear of God.
If anyone eagerly wishes to turn from wrong-doing back to right behaviour, one is to be merciful to him very readily, as best one can, for the fear of God.
Und wenn einer willig von Unrecht wieder zur Rechtsordnung umkehren will, so erbarme man sich aus Gottesfurcht, wie man bestens vermag, dessen recht willig.
And if anyone is willing to turn back from wrong to the order of law, let one take pity, out of fear of God, as best one can, very willingly on him.
div.note: G's ‘best’ was altered to ‘betst’ in G (archaising, Liebermann says).
man for: man him for B
mæge: B adds, then crosses out, ðam men
